speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the physical characteristics of your enlarged supraclavicular lymph node, such as whether it is hard, fixed, or tender, and tell me how long these symptoms have been present.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of significant weight loss, drenching night sweats, and worsening abdominal pain alongside the supraclavicular lymphadenopathy are very concerning for a malignancy like lymphoma or metastatic cancer. Can you tell me if you have noticed any lumps in your neck, armpits, or groin, and do you have a history of smoking or alcohol use?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malignancy (Suspected Lymphoma or Metastatic Carcinoma)

The combination of "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss), a hard and fixed supraclavicular lymph node, and abdominal pain is highly concerning for malignancy. We need to proceed immediately with imaging and tissue sampling to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST IMAGES: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis
REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, LDH, and CA 19-9/CEA
REQUEST TEST: Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) of the supraclavicular node
